subject: OpenAI Jalapeño Chip 🔧, Anthropic Claude Unified Memory 🧠, Perplexity
intro: Today's theme is simple: memory and infrastructure are the new moat. OpenAI built its own inference chip in nine months using its own AI. Anthropic gave Claude unified memory across chat and agents. Prime Intellect open-sourced a harness that lets models reuse context across runs. Three different bets, same conviction: the next edge isn't the model, it's the stack around it. We're watching the industry quietly shift from "who has the best weights" to "who controls the full loop."

news.headline: OpenAI's custom inference chip promises faster ChatGPT and lower costs
news.body: OpenAI just showed off real benchmark results for Jalapeño , its first custom chip built specifically to run AI models, not train them. Think of inference as the moment ChatGPT actually writes your reply. That is what this chip is built for. It was co-built with Broadcom and went from design to finished chip in just nine months, partly because OpenAI used its own AI models to help design it. Here is what makes it interesting: For you, this means faster Codex responses, snappier ChatGPT , and fewer slowdowns as usage grows. You cannot rent or buy this chip. It runs OpenAI's infrastructure only.
bullets: Targets ~50% lower cost per response compared to Nvidia's current best chips
Handles both speed and volume without trading one for the other, something most chips struggle with
Keeps the model's short-term memory close to the processor, so less data travels around and replies come back faster
A Gen 2 is already deep in development, Gen 3 is taking shape

news.headline: Anthropic gives Claude persistent memory across all chats by default
news.body: You know that annoying thing where you explain your whole project setup to Claude in chat, then switch to Claude Cowork (the AI agent that handles multi-step tasks like building docs or running code), and it has zero clue what you just said? That's fixed. Claude now shares one unified memory across both chat and Cowork. Context you built up in chat is instantly available when Cowork runs a task, and vice versa. No more rebriefing. Here's what you can actually do with it: It's on by default on Free, Pro, and Max plans. You're in full control of what stays.
bullets: Say "remember this" mid-chat to save something specific
Go to Settings > Memory to read, edit, or delete anything Claude has saved
Enable sensitive topics (health, beliefs) manually if you want that context saved too
Memory updates live during conversations, not just after they end

news.headline: Perplexity ships fully local AI agent that runs on NVIDIA DGX Spark
news.body: Perplexity just shipped Portable Computer , and the core idea is simple: your AI agent runs entirely on your own machine. No cloud. No data leaving your desk. Until now, every Perplexity agent ran on remote servers. Portable Computer flips that. The orchestrator (the brain that plans tasks), the subagent (the part that executes them), and the full tool harness all run locally on your hardware. Here is what that unlocks: It runs on the NVIDIA DGX Spark with either PPLX 27B or Qwen 3.8 27B. Setup is one click inside the Perplexity app. Available now for Pro and Max subscribers on Linux.
bullets: Zero token costs for local tasks. Long loops, big file analysis, repo-scale work, all free.
Your sensitive files never leave your device. PII is flagged automatically.
Cloud escalation is opt-in, per step, with your approval each time.
Connects to Google Drive, Gmail, GitHub, and Slack.
